faq.q: What's the difference between joules and calories for energy measurement?
faq.a: Joules are the SI (International System) unit for energy used in scientific and engineering applications, while calories measure thermal energy, particularly in food and nutrition. 1 calorie equals exactly 4.184 joules. Our energy converter handles both units with precise calculations for all applications.

faq.q: How do I convert kilowatt-hours (kWh) to joules?
faq.a: 1 kilowatt-hour equals exactly 3,600,000 joules (3.6 megajoules). To convert kWh to joules, multiply the kWh value by 3,600,000. For example, 5 kWh = 18,000,000 joules. Our energy converter performs this calculation automatically with full precision.

faq.q: What are BTUs used for in energy calculations?
faq.a: BTUs (British Thermal Units) are commonly used in heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) systems to measure thermal energy. 1 BTU equals approximately 1,055 joules. BTUs are standard in HVAC system ratings, furnace capacity, and cooling system specifications.

faq.q: Which energy unit should I use for different applications?
faq.a: Use joules for scientific calculations and SI unit systems, kWh for electrical energy consumption and utility billing, calories for food energy and nutrition, BTUs for HVAC and thermal systems, and foot-pounds for mechanical energy in imperial systems.

faq.q: How accurate is the energy converter for professional use?
faq.a: Our energy converter uses exact international conversion factors and maintains high decimal precision, making it suitable for engineering calculations, scientific research, HVAC system design, and professional energy analysis applications.

faq.q: Can I convert between different types of energy units?
faq.a: Yes, our energy converter handles all major energy units including thermal energy (BTU, calories), electrical energy (kWh, joules), and mechanical energy (foot-pounds) with accurate cross-conversions between different energy measurement systems.
